specification_compliance: The route clip_covers.py follows note_openings.py for the filter-file-ids → /files/bulk → drive + TEXT_MIMES gate, as step 14 requires (I6). The loft:// check uses a second bulk call filtered by drive and file_type=image, and on failure it degrades to image_id=null.
For I1, clipConditions() fixes type=text and origin=webclip after the target's params. Recently opened is the only shelf asked without the target.
For I11 and SPEC-ADDON-100 I27, the ClipSection region stays mounted across views in pages/clips.tsx. blockedFor is keyed by nickname, so the viewer block lifts when the nickname changes.
For I8, ClipCard reserves an aspect-[4/3] cover box, a min-h title area and a min-h-4 meta line before the cover answer arrives.
potential_unspecified_behavior: When the frontmatter is invalid YAML, or runs past the 4096-byte read so its closing `---` is never seen, frontmatter.parse returns the whole text as the body. extract_cover then reads URLs inside the frontmatter as body links for the site. Step 14 and I7 are silent on this case.

When a shelf page's refresh re-asks several pages, it drops drawn cards those pages no longer name, unless the card is being saved (usePagedClips.ts:103-106). Step 5 says only that later pages already drawn stay.
regression_risks: The shared e2e fetch stub (fixtures/app.tsx) now sends traffic through the Clips handlers before every other route. Only the location.hash guards keep that traffic away from the other arrangements.
pages/clips.tsx now depends on the Notes library hook `../library/useScopedLoad` and on `notesapp/useNotesTarget`. A change to either would now reach Clips too.
test_coverage: No core test pins TargetMenu's `defaultTargetOrigin`, or the unchanged request when the prop is absent (I10). See R6.
The backend parser is covered by two overlapping files, test_clip_covers.py and test_clip_covers_acceptance.py. Neither covers a frontmatter that is unterminated within 4096 bytes.
not_verified: I did not run any test, vitest, pytest or Playwright. The read-only tools cannot execute them.

I did not check whether the core inventory tests the touch points list (ime-enter-guard, page-headings, section-headings, line-clamp-display, escape-listeners, page-container-width, componentFixtureParity, check-coverage-denominator) needed updates for the new clipsapp files.
I did not check that PageTabs accepts the `wrap` prop, or that useScopedLoad keeps its old data on a failed refresh.
I did not check whether the core /files/bulk excludes trashed files. I assumed it matches note-openings.
